newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-DE SILVA LEAD SRI LANKA FIGHTBACK.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-DE SILVA LEAD SRI LANKA FIGHTBACK.

text.p: Aravinda de Silva led a Sri Lankan fightback against Pakistan with a stylish century on the first day of the second and final test match on Saturday.

De Silva was in superb form at one end as wickets fell regularly at the other, finishing the day unbeaten on 101, his second successive century in the current series, as Sri Lanka reached 281 for seven.
De Silva hit 15 fours in his chanceless innings, piercing the field regularly, after Pakistani bowlers had battled back strongly in the afternoon session to claim five Sri Lankan wickets.
His first fifty came off 72 balls and his second required only 47. It was De Silva's 10th test century and his sixth against Pakistan.
Without De Silva and opener Sanath Jayasuriya, who made a quick 72 off 96 balls, Sri Lanka's decision to bat first after winning the toss might have backfired.
Following a record first wicket partnership against Pakistan of 95 between Jayasuriya and Russell Arnold, the Sri Lanka middle-order collapsed as Pakistan's attack bowled tightly.
Jayasuriya was the first to go soon after lunch. He added only one run to his interval score of 71 before being caught by Mushtaq at first slip attempting to cut Saqlain.

Maravan Atapattu quickly followed, caught at silly point for 14, before Arnold was run out after being called for a sharp single by Aravinda De Silva. Arnold batted for 183 minutes for his 37, which included four boundaries.

Saqlain then took the prize wicket of captain Arjuna Ranatunga for four to leave Sri Lanka tottering, and their position worsened when Hashan Tillekeratne was bowled by a quick delivery from paceman Mohammed Zahid when he had scored 10.
De Silva and Kaluwitharana stabilised the innings by adding 60 for the sixth wicket and Chaminda Vaas then helped his senior partner add an unbeaten 57 for the eighth wicket.
Saqlain, who took nine wickets in the first test, was again the best Pakistani bowler and finished the day with 3 for 93 in 34 overs.
